title: Twistor helical vertical bitlines cancel 3D coupling noise
idea: The twistor wound magnetic tape helically around a wire to define its sensing path. Shift each vertical 3D DRAM bitline a quarter pitch at every tier step, so it climbs in a staircase helix and spends equal length beside each neighbor. Coupling then becomes common-mode, which the differential sense amp rejects.
why: Cuts inter-bitline coupling noise ~3-5x in 3D stacks (fact 2), allowing smaller signals and more tiers per sense amp.

title: Negative-capacitance ferroelectric film as bitline signal amplifier
idea: Insert a thin doped-HfO2 negative-capacitance layer in series at the SA input gate (or at the bitline contact), capacitance-matched so the charge-sharing step has voltage gain above 1 and amplifies the cell signal before the latch fires.
why: Capacitor wall (fact 1): 2-3x signal gain would let Cs drop to ~2 fF and permit lower VARY (fact 10).

title: Token-ring wordline sequencer for append-only KV-cache mats
idea: KV-caches append and stream tokens in order, so dedicated mats replace the row decoder with a token passed along a chain of shift-register stages (one per 8 wordlines plus a 3-bit local predecoder), allowing random access only at block granularity. Everything is drawn at DUV pitch.
why: Row-decoder area -60% in AI-tier mats with no EUV-pitch decoders, matched to KV-cache access patterns.

title: Po: one amplifier hears sixteen bitlines via CCD transfer
idea: Po: bitlines without sense amps. Borrow CCD readout: short bitlines end in a buried-channel charge-transfer register that clocks each cell's charge packet losslessly to a floating-diffusion amplifier shared by 16 bitlines, which senses it non-destructively and writes it back through the reverse transfer.
why: Periphery (#7) and capacitor wall (#1): 16:1 fewer sense circuits, and charge-domain readout is not divided by bitline capacitance, so the full Cs charge is sensed; transfer time (~0.5 ns/stage) is the price.

title: Delete plate-line drivers: bitline-only bipolar FeRAM drive
idea: Constraint: non-volatile 1T1C ferroelectric, without FeRAM's large, slow plate-line drivers. Tie all plates to a fixed mid-rail and switch polarization by driving the bitline to +V or -V around it (bipolar bitline drivers built into the SA), so the plate needs no driver and no decoding.
why: Periphery area -8-12% and ~2x faster cycles (plate RC was the bottleneck); plate energy disappears.

title: NEMS relay wordline drivers with zero off-leakage
idea: Ruthenium-contact nanoelectromechanical relays are built in BEOL at <=350 C with a sacrificial release and used as mat-select and wordline-driver switches: they pass 3 V natively, need no level shifters or stacked high-voltage transistors, and leak nothing when open.
why: Facts 7 and 10: wordline-driver area MINIFIED 2-3x and standby leakage to ~0, tungsten-free; contact wear and ~10 ns mechanical delay are the risks.

title: Power-fail dump: every sense amp owns a vertical NV backup string
idea: Constraint: DRAM data must survive power loss without giving up DRAM endurance. Under each SA stripe, a hybrid-bonded layer gives every sense amp its own short FeFET or charge-trap string; on power-fail detect, all banks open rows in lockstep and ~2M SAs per die program their bits in parallel, dumping 32 Gb in ~1 ms from on-package capacitors, then restore through the same SAs at power-up.
why: NV DRAM with no NVDIMM flash controller or battery; backup parallelism ~1000x NVDIMM-N, and the NV layer sees one write per power cycle, so its endurance is irrelevant.

title: Foldable-phone flex hinge folds periphery behind the array
idea: Borrowed from foldable phones and flex-PCB folding: array and periphery are built side by side on polyimide, then the periphery strip is folded 180 degrees behind the array through a thin bent interconnect zone, so it takes no footprint and sits ~20 um under its mats.
why: Periphery ~49% (fact 7): footprint array efficiency rises toward ~90% with short vertical links, without wafer bonding or TSVs.

title: Each cell is its own sense amp: stacked oxide latches
idea: Inverting 'storage and amplification are separate': each bit is a 4-transistor cross-coupled latch of n-IGZO and p-SnO thin-film transistors stacked in 8 BEOL tiers, so the cell itself drives the bitline rail-to-rail and per-bitline sense amps shrink to one shared buffer per 256 columns.
why: Deletes sense-amp stripes (~20% of die) and refresh entirely, with tiers recovering density; oxide leakage keeps static power tiny. No capacitor anywhere.

title: Predictive-coding memory link transmitting only prediction errors
idea: The visual cortex sends mostly prediction errors, not raw images. Identical lightweight predictors (last-value, stride, zero-run) sit at both ends of a CXL/DIMM link on FPGA, and only the entropy-coded XOR residual crosses the wire. FPGA prototype, ~$600k in 18 months.
why: Fact 5: residuals are mostly zeros, so ~1.5-2x fewer bits cross a 10-20 pJ/bit link. That buys effective bandwidth and energy and lets fewer channels feed the same compute.

title: Leakage-replica decay timer sets refresh interval automatically
idea: Effect: junction/GIDL leakage tracking in replica cells. Each mat holds a few replica storage cells with ~4x smaller capacitance, charged at every refresh and watched by a comparator; because they leak through the same physics as data cells, their threshold crossing marks a self-timed refresh deadline that follows process, voltage and temperature.
why: Refresh (fact 3): typical dies can refresh ~2-4x less often than the fixed worst-case spec; fits a small team's gain-cell/eDRAM macro on MPW.

title: Time-to-digital readout turns DRAM cells into two-bit cells
idea: Inverting 'a bit is one voltage compared once': after charge sharing, each bitline discharges through a cell-voltage-controlled current source and a time-to-digital converter shared by 64 columns timestamps the threshold crossing, resolving four stored charge levels per cell.
why: 2 bits per capacitor gives ~2x density without new lithography; the shared TDC adds <10% periphery. Multi-level charge margins against leakage are the hard part.

title: Si: silicone block-copolymer self-assembly patterns regular decoder gratings
idea: Redesign decoders and sub-wordline drivers as strictly periodic gratings patterned by PS-b-PDMS directed self-assembly; the silicon-rich PDMS block becomes a SiOx hardmask in an O2/H2 plasma with no argon, and a coarse guide pattern from a non-excimer tool sets registration.
why: Replaces several neon-dependent ArF multipatterning exposures in periphery with ~10 nm self-assembly, cutting masks and capital (fact 4).

title: RF reflectometry reads bitlines through on-chip LC resonators
idea: Substitute DC charge-sharing readout with RF reflectometry, as used for qubit readout: each bitline is part of a spiral-inductor LC tank whose MOS-varactor tuning depends on the cell charge, and a frequency-multiplexed probe tone reads many bitlines on one line from phase shifts.
why: Periphery area: frequency multiplexing lets one RF readout chain serve dozens of bitlines, replacing pitch-matched latches.

title: Wafer-scale memory slab: one periphery per quadrant, no packaging
idea: Reverse die and wafer: a whole U.S.-fabbed 300 mm array wafer becomes one memory appliance with stitched global buses, redundant reticle tiles and one shared periphery/I/O tile per quadrant, mounted directly on a U.S.-made cold plate with no dicing or offshore packaging.
why: Fact 7 and U.S. manufacturability: per-die pads, I/O and ESD (~10%) amortized; Asian OSAT dependency removed; ~TB per wafer.

title: Eliminate multi-patterning in sense-amp stripes via block-copolymer self-assembly
idea: SA and column-select transistor arrays are periodic at bitline pitch, so define their gate and active lines by directed self-assembly of PS-b-PMMA guided by coarse KrF chemical prepatterns. Remove the PMMA with UV plus an acetic acid rinse and transfer with HBr/Cl2/O2, eliminating fluorocarbon SADP spacer etches and PAG resists.
why: Pitch-matched SAs below 30 nm without EUV or SADP (fact 4); SA-stripe patterning cost ~-40-60%.

title: Retinal center-surround sense amp referencing six averaged neighbour bitlines
idea: Like retinal horizontal cells that subtract the local mean, each sense amp compares its bitline against the capacitively averaged voltage of six unselected bitlines in the adjacent mat (a passive BEOL coupling-cap network switched in during sensing), so wordline coupling, plate bounce and substrate noise cancel as common mode. Averaging six references cuts reference noise by about 2.4x versus one.
why: Fact 1 capacitor wall: common-mode noise and reference mismatch eat ~30-40% of sense margin; cancelling it could let Cs drop from ~5 fF to ~3 fF, so capacitor AR falls from 60-75:1 to ~40:1 with fewer etch/deposition steps.

title: Skipper-CCD repeated non-destructive sampling of gain-cell charge
idea: Borrowed from dark-matter Skipper CCDs that measure one charge packet hundreds of times: a gain cell's storage node gates a floating-gate sense transistor that a column-parallel integrator samples 16-64 times without disturbing the charge, averaging noise down by sqrt(N). Cells holding only ~200-500 electrons (0.03-0.08 fF) become reliably readable.
why: Capacitor charge wall (fact 1): required storage charge drops 10-50x, freeing planar or capacitor-less cells from 60-75:1 pillars; cost is ~5-15 ns extra read latency.

title: Shopkeeper's open recipe: public pitch-matched periphery compiler
idea: A shopkeeper sells flour, not only finished bread. Fund an open generator for pitch-matched sense amps, sub-wordline drivers, fuse boxes and DDR5/HBM PHYs, qualified to JEDEC specs, so new U.S. DRAM entrants spend effort on the array, not on decades of hidden periphery know-how.
why: Cuts design cost and time to market for new fabs (capital, U.S. manufacturability); periphery is ~49% of die and most of the tacit knowledge (fact 7).

title: Homogeneity: n-type-only oxide periphery built with the array masks
idea: TRIZ #33 Homogeneity: every periphery circuit uses the same n-type IGZO TFT as the array, with bootstrapped dynamic logic, pseudo-differential charge-transfer sense amps and capacitive level shifters, so the whole chip, array plus periphery, needs ~8-10 masks with no wells or implants and can be repeated tier after tier.
why: 100x path: ~8x fewer masks than 60-80-mask DRAM, no EUV, and periphery repeated in each stacked tier keeps tiers independent and testable; trade-offs: ~10x slower periphery (us-class) and higher dynamic power. Attacks Facts 4 and 7 and U.S. manufacturability.

title: Po: shrink the capacitor to amplify — MOS varactor parametric gain
idea: Po: an amplifier with no gain transistor. Sample the bitline differential onto a pair of silicon MOS varactors held in accumulation, then pulse them into depletion so their capacitance falls ~5x while charge is conserved, raising the differential voltage ~5x before the latch.
why: Capacitor wall (#1) and periphery (#7): ~5x voltage gain before any matched transistor, so SA offset matters ~5x less; silicon and oxide only.

title: Mise-en-place decoding: arm wordline drivers on ACT's first cycle
idea: A chef preps before the full order arrives. DDR5's ACT spans two command cycles; the die decodes bank and upper row bits from the first cycle and pre-boosts the selected mat's wordline-driver group, finishing the lower bits on the second cycle.
why: Frees ~1-2 ns of internal tRCD slack, spent on smaller, lower-leakage decoder devices or lower VPP (facts 7, 10).

title: Termite-mound chimney DIMM shroud enabling refresh downshift
idea: Termite mounds hold steady temperatures with passive convection chimneys. 3D-printed DIMM shrouds with mound-like chimney and tunnel geometry use existing server airflow to keep DRAM under ~45 C. A BIOS policy, keyed to the on-DIMM temperature sensor, leaves 2x refresh mode and stretches refresh when the sensor confirms cool operation. CFD plus prototypes, ~$300k in 12 months.
why: Fact 3: retention roughly doubles per ~10 C. Running ~15 C cooler avoids 2x refresh and cuts refresh energy and bandwidth loss ~50%.

title: Light-addressed wordlines with photoconductive access devices
idea: Box: stacked cap x photoconductive access (a-Si:H or MoS2) x electrical SA x bonded photonic layer x Si plus SiN waveguides x photonic foundry. Each row's access devices sit under a waveguide; a light pulse routed by an on-chip optical switch tree turns the row on, so no row decoders, 3 V wordline drivers or VPP pumps are needed, and dark access devices barely leak.
why: Periphery: row decode/drive area and wordline CV^2 energy removed; row hammer gone because there is no wordline coupling.

title: Po: the periphery is the product — open bonded interface
idea: Po: a DRAM company that makes no memory cells. Define an open JEDEC-style hybrid-bonding contract between array wafers and periphery wafers (pad map, analog bitline/wordline electrical specs, timing), so any foundry or new U.S. entrant can build periphery dies that pair with any vendor's array wafers.
why: Capital (#4) and U.S. manufacturability: periphery needs mature logic fabs, not $15B DRAM fabs; opens the ~49% periphery share of the die to competition and second sourcing.

title: O: electrochemically anodized gate oxides for room-temperature periphery transistors
idea: Anodize Zr or Al gate metal in an aqueous electrolyte so oxygen from water grows a self-limited ZrO2 or Al2O3 gate dielectric whose thickness is set by voltage (~1-2 nm/V), building BEOL periphery transistors without plasma ALD or argon sputtering.
why: Atomic-scale thickness control without vacuum tools enables cheap low-temperature periphery tiers over the array (facts 4, 7).

title: Plated-pillar magnetic memory: coincident-current writes, inductive non-destructive reads
idea: Failure mined: plated-wire memory (UNIVAC, Apollo era) read magnetic bits non-destructively with no per-bit transistor but died on hand-assembled wire. Fix: build it monolithically by ALD-coating vertical pillars with a soft magnetic film inside a stack of deposited word planes. Coincident currents in a plane and a pillar write one intersection, and a plane pulse rotates the film so the pillar picks up an inductive or AMR signal without erasing the bit.
why: 10x at the same cost: a transistorless 4F^2 cell per tier and 32 tiers from one hole etch, with unlimited magnetic endurance and no refresh, ~15x bits/mm^2. Periphery scales per plane and per pillar, not per bit.

title: Neuristor Mott lines self-regenerate global wordlines
idea: Revive Crane's 1960 neuristor, an active line that propagates pulses without loss. NbO2 Mott-threshold elements with local shunt capacitors are spaced along long global wordlines and data lines, so the pulse re-fires at each element the way an action potential travels down an axon, and no CMOS repeaters are needed.
why: Removes repeater and buffer stripes (fact 7) and cuts energy on long global lines ~2x (fact 5).

title: 2050 trim: ferroelectric offset memory inside every sense amp
idea: A 2050 engineer would never accept factory-random mismatch. Insert a ~30 nm HZO capacitor at each SA latch node, programmed once at wafer test to a polarization that cancels that SA's measured offset and retained for years.
why: Offset drops from ~15 mV to ~3 mV, so bitlines can double (half the SA stripes, ~7% die) or Cs can shrink ~40% (facts 1, 7).

title: Barn-owl Jeffress delay-line coincidence decoder on one wire pair
idea: Barn owls localize sound with counter-propagating axonal delay lines and coincidence-detector neurons. Pulses launch from both ends of a tapped delay-chain select wire, with their relative launch time encoding the row address. Only the driver where they meet sees both pulses inside its coincidence window and fires.
why: Fact 7: one wire pair plus a programmable launch delay replaces a multi-level decoder tree and predecode buses for 64-256 drivers, cutting decode area ~40% and decode energy.

title: Predecoder XOR key rotates the row map each epoch
idea: Add a 16-bit XOR stage to the row predecoder whose key is re-randomized every refresh window, migrating data row by row during the refresh walk that already reads and restores every row, so an attacker's physical neighbors change unpredictably and hammer counts never accumulate on fixed victims.
why: Row hammer (fact 9): defeats targeted ~1k-activation attacks without large counter tables; a gates-only change any old node can build.

title: Eliminate silicon oxide and nitride etching: chlorine-etchable periphery dielectrics
idea: In the periphery, swap the SiO2 and SiN that practically require fluorocarbon or HF to etch for dielectrics that etch in Cl/Br plasma or mild wet chemistry: Al2O3 and HfO2 (BCl3/Cl2), AlN (Cl2 or hot KOH) and amorphous-carbon hard masks (O2). SiO2 stays only where it is never etched (gap fill, lift-off).
why: Gives a fully fluorine-free periphery palette; Al2O3 and AlN also conduct heat ~10-100x better than SiO2. Their higher k is offset by air gaps.

title: OS-visible elastic capacity retires failed mats instead of modules
idea: Ideal result: memory that degrades by grams, not kilograms. Periphery reports failed or weak mats through a standard interface, and the OS offlines just those address ranges, shrinking capacity by a fraction of a percent per fault.
why: Keeps modules in service for years, raising usable supply.

title: Guard-driven bitline shields borrowed from femtoamp electrometers
idea: Scale the lab electrometer's driven guard down to the bitline: a 2-transistor follower in the bonded CMOS tier drives a shield trace beside each bitline to the bitline's own voltage during charge sharing, so bitline-to-neighbor and bitline-to-plate capacitance sees almost no voltage and stops soaking up signal.
why: Effective Cbl falls ~30-45%, so either Cs drops ~1.5x (fact 1) or bitlines double in length and SA stripes halve (fact 7).

title: Voltage-stacked mats recycle bitline charge through series domains
idea: Space and implant power systems stack loads in series: two mats sit between 2 V and ground with a 1 V mid-rail, so charge that discharges the upper mat's bitlines then charges the lower mat's. A scheduler pairs activations to keep the stack balanced.
why: Bitline energy drawn from the supply roughly halved (fact 10), with simpler regulators and only DUV circuitry.

title: Ping-pong sense-enable drivers reverse current for electromigration healing
idea: Black's law makes Cu EM life ~19x shorter at 125 C than 85 C (Ea~0.9 eV), forcing wide SAN/SAP rails. Drive these rails from alternating ends on successive activations so current direction reverses, giving AC-like bidirectional stress with ~10x longer EM life.
why: Periphery area (fact 7): sense-enable and VARY straps can be ~2-3x narrower while meeting 10 y at 125 C.

title: Egg grading: on-die margin sweep sells refresh-grade memory tiers
idea: Grade dies like eggs (AA, A, B): every die runs an on-die sweep of SA reference offset steps and retention waits, then is sold as a 'cool-datacenter' grade (256 ms refresh at <=60 C), a standard grade or a 'hot' grade; operators who run cold buy parts needing 4x less refresh.
why: Usable supply and refresh tax (fact 3): turns retention spread into priced tiers, recovering 10-20% bandwidth on graded parts and monetizing margin now wasted on worst-case design.

title: IGZO-isolated charge-transfer preamp enables 2048-cell bitlines
idea: Box: 1T1C x Si access x charge-transfer preamplifier x local isolation x bulk Si x BEOL IGZO switch. A gate-biased transfer transistor holds the bitline at a fixed potential while the cell charge is pushed onto a tiny sense node (gain ~Cbl/Csn ~10x), and an ultra-low-leakage IGZO switch isolates that node so the signal survives.
why: Bitlines 4x longer and SA count /4 (periphery ~-15% of die); bitline swing energy also drops.

title: Charge-pump capacitors move into six BEOL MIM levels
idea: ALD ZrO2/HfO2 MIM capacitors (250-300 C) stacked in six upper metal levels MAGNIFY pump capacitance per footprint ~6x, so pumps run at lower frequency with higher efficiency and their silicon area is freed for cells.
why: Facts 7 and 10: ~3-4% die area reclaimed and VPP efficiency +15-20 points.

title: Beforehand cushioning: NAND-grade LDPC lets sense amps run at 1e-3 errors
idea: TRIZ #11 Beforehand cushioning: a 4 KB-codeword LDPC decoder with soft-read support in the base die absorbs raw bit error rates up to ~1e-3, so sense amps can be minimum-size latches with large offset, cells ~2x smaller, and 2-bit multilevel storage practical.
why: 100x path: ~2x periphery shrink, ~2x cell shrink and ~2x bits per cell compound with stacking; trade-offs: ~0.5-2 us decode latency, 4 KB access granularity and ~10% parity overhead. Attacks Facts 1 and 7.

title: Eliminate VDD/2 precharge: plate-pulsed sensing from grounded bitlines
idea: Hold bitlines at ground and delete the equalizer transistors and the VBLP generator. To read, pulse the segmented cell plate of the selected 512-cell sub-array upward (FeRAM-style plate-line drive). A '1' cell pushes more charge onto the floating bitline than a '0', against a half-plate-pulse dummy reference, and a ground-referenced NMOS stage resolves it.
why: Removes precharge/equalize current (~15-20% of activate energy) and the VBLP regulator (~1-2% area); a ground-precharged bitline also eases low-voltage operation (fact 10).

title: Silicon switched-capacitor PMIC replaces on-die charge pumps
idea: Reverse where high rails are made: VPP, VBB and VARY come from a U.S.-fabbed silicon switched-capacitor converter on the module, fed through bumps; silicon is chosen over GaN because gallium is ~98% Chinese.
why: Facts 7 and 10: ~5-8% die area recovered and pump efficiency ~30% -> ~85%, cutting VPP energy ~2.5x.

title: One roving spare sense amp covers any failed column
idea: Ideal result: one spare that is everywhere. A single fast spare SA per mat is time-shared through a column steering bus with per-column sample capacitors; when built-in self-test finds a dead SA, the spare substitutes, and its assignment moves as new faults appear.
why: Repair cost: cuts redundant-column area overhead ~3-5x versus fixed spare columns.

title: Electrometer-style active guard bootstraps away bitline capacitance
idea: Parasitic capacitance only steals signal if its far plate moves differently from the bitline. Run a shield conductor between/under bitlines driven by a unity-gain bootstrap buffer that follows the bitline pair's common node (the electrometer guard trick), cutting effective Cbl ~5x.
why: Signal = Q/(Cs+Cbl_eff): ~4-5x more signal or ~4x smaller Cs at equal margin (fact 1); allows 2-4x longer bitlines, halving SA count (fact 7).

title: Palo Verde model: periphery chiplet fab running on reclaimed sewage
idea: Arizona's Palo Verde nuclear plant cools with treated municipal wastewater instead of freshwater. Site a U.S. periphery/logic-chiplet fab beside a city wastewater plant, take tertiary effluent as UPW feedstock, run zero-liquid-discharge with air-cooled chillers, and contract long-term effluent rights.
why: Water: freshwater withdrawal per wafer falls >10x (effluent replaces potable supply, ZLD recovers ~90%), easing Southwest permits and U.S. siting.

title: Half-volt array: 0.5 V VARY with 1% sensing failures
idea: Box: standard cap x Si access x high-gain SA x low-voltage array domain x bulk Si x standard. Bitline/cell voltage drops from ~1 V to 0.5 V and the wordline from ~3 V to ~2.2 V; the halved signal mis-senses ~1% of bits, which the code repairs.
why: Voltage floor: array CV^2 energy ~-4x, smaller pumps, less wordline stress.

title: Eliminate temperature sensors and refresh timers: canary-row retention sentinels
idea: Delete the on-die thermal sensors, refresh-rate tables and fixed 64 ms timer. Each bank instead holds 4 canary rows built with ~60% of normal Cs, checked periodically, and the bank refreshes only when a canary loses its pattern. Refresh then tracks actual leakage, including the 13 fA tail, at the current temperature and voltage.
why: Fact 3: refresh is 16-33% of idle power. Under typical conditions the refresh rate falls 4-8x while worst-case cells stay guarded, and the thermal-sensor and ADC area goes away.

title: U.S. mature logic fabs build control dies; DRAM fabs only arrays
idea: Worse: build control periphery on scarce, EUV-laden DRAM wafer starts. Flip: contract control, I/O, pump and test dies to U.S. 28-40 nm logic foundries and hybrid-bond them to array-dense dies from DRAM fabs that keep only bitline sense amps and spend the rest of the wafer on bits.
why: Capital intensity and supply: ~30-40% more bits per DRAM-fab wafer start, using underused U.S. logic capacity.

title: Scrap-yard LRDIMM: data buffers steer around dead banks
idea: An embargoed engineer rebuilds working machines from rejects. Dies whose only failure is one bank's sense-amp stripe or decoder are paired on an LRDIMM with a spare die; the RCD and data buffers redirect that bank's commands and DQ lanes to the spare, so the host sees a normal DDR5 rank.
why: Recovers dies scrapped for periphery defects (several % of output), raising usable supply without a new fab.

title: Eliminate the VPP charge pump with a shared bootstrap boost plate
idea: Run a common boost plate under all wordlines of a sub-array. The decoder drives the selected wordline to VDD (1.1 V) and floats it, while all unselected wordlines stay actively clamped low. A 1.1 V step on the boost plate then couples only the floating wordline up to ~2.8 V for the restore window, as in a bootstrapped driver.
why: Removes the VPP pumps (~3-5% of die, 30-40% efficient) and roughly halves wordline energy, because the boost charge comes from a single 1.1 V swing (facts 7 and 10).

title: Excessive action: 256-tier vertical bitline read by chopper auto-zero amplifier
idea: TRIZ #16 Excessive action: one vertical bitline is deliberately overloaded with 256 tiers of planar ~1 fF thin-film capacitor cells (bitline ~300 fF, signal ~1.5 mV) and read by a chopper-stabilized, auto-zeroed, correlated-double-sampling amplifier under the array that integrates for ~1 us, so one amplifier serves 256 stacked cells.
why: 100x path: no high-aspect-ratio capacitor module, no EUV, periphery ~2% of die and BEOL-repeatable tiers; trade-offs: microsecond reads, kT/C noise holds SNR near ~10 so cells must stay at ~1 fF or more, and higher sense energy. Attacks Facts 1, 2 and 7.

title: Al: aluminum-polysilicon thermocouple mesh sets per-subarray refresh rates
idea: Lay Al / n+ poly-Si Seebeck junctions (Al by thermal evaporation, poly by LPCVD, no argon sputter) across the die; their uV/K outputs feed a shared chopper ADC so each subarray's refresh interval follows its own local temperature instead of the hottest spot.
why: Refresh is sized for worst-case temperature; hot-spot-aware refresh can cut refresh ops ~30-50% in cooler regions (fact 3) with near-zero-power sensors.

title: Token-passing shift-chain wordline sequencer for streaming weight memory
idea: Substitute the random-access row decoder with a one-flop-per-wordline token chain that steps to the next row on each activate, plus a coarse jump decoder every 64 rows. This targets AI weight and KV streaming, where row order is known.
why: Periphery area: row decode logic shrinks ~60% and wordline select energy drops to one flop toggle; fits HBM-class AI memory, where streaming dominates.

title: Feedback: time-to-resolve margin meter schedules per-row refresh
idea: TRIZ #23 Feedback: a shared completion detector measures how long each sense amp takes to resolve during refresh; rows whose bits resolve slowly (low remaining charge) are logged in a small per-bank weak-row table and refreshed sooner, while fast-resolving rows stretch their interval to 256 ms or more.
why: Fact 3: refresh energy and bandwidth ~-50-70% because only measured-weak rows get the fast rate, with no pre-test retention profiling.

title: Po: bitlines are the pump — idle-bank flying capacitors
idea: Po: a charge pump built from the memory's own wires. In idle banks, groups of bitlines (~100 fF each, millions available) are reconfigured through the equalizer switches plus a few added series switches into a switched-capacitor ladder that stacks charge up to VPP for the active banks' wordlines.
why: Periphery (#7): deletes most dedicated pump capacitor area by reusing capacitance already paid for; silicon only.

title: Ferroelectric negative-capacitance layer cancels bitline parasitic capacitance
idea: Effect: ferroelectric negative capacitance. Hang a stabilized HZO/dielectric NC capacitor in parallel on each bitline sense node, tuned so the net node capacitance stays positive but drops ~2x. The charge-transfer ratio Cs/(Cs+CBL) roughly doubles.
why: Capacitor wall (fact 1): halves the Cs needed (AR ~70:1 to ~40:1), or doubles cells per bitline so half the SA stripes are needed.

title: Mo: molybdenum-chloride CVD replaces tungsten in periphery contacts
idea: Fill periphery contacts and wordline straps with Mo from MoO2Cl2 and H2 CVD (H2 carrier, N2 purge, no argon) instead of WF6 tungsten; Mo's short electron mean free path lowers resistance in narrow lines.
why: Lower resistance lets drivers shrink (fact 7) and removes the China-dominated tungsten chokepoint from periphery metallization.

title: Spin-to-charge sign readout instead of measuring resistance
idea: Inverting 'magnetic bits are read by their resistance magnitude': a small supply current through each nanomagnet into a heavy-metal/oxide interface produces an inverse Rashba-Edelstein voltage whose sign follows the magnetization, and that signed voltage directly drives the gate of a single sense transistor.
why: Sign detection needs no reference and no TMR margin, so the sense amp collapses to one transistor and read disturb vanishes; capacitor-free.

title: Bipolar-input sense amps on bonded SiGe BiCMOS die
idea: Bond array wafers to 130 nm SiGe BiCMOS periphery wafers, where bipolar input pairs (Vbe matching ~1 mV versus ~10-20 mV for small MOSFETs) sense bitlines through an 8:1 column mux, reading groups in rapid sequence.
why: Capacitor wall (fact 1): 5-10x lower offset allows ~3x smaller Cs or ~4x longer bitlines, using idle trailing BiCMOS fabs.

title: Sense amps on the wafer backside via U.S. backside flow
idea: Rearrange the faces: using a U.S.-developed backside-processing flow (the kind built for backside power), the array occupies the front, the wafer is thinned, and SAs and wordline drivers are built on the back, joined to bitline groups by nano-TSVs.
why: Fact 7: the front side holds only cells (die ~-30-40%), and the backside also carries power, freeing front metal.

title: Event-camera address-event bus for self-requested refresh
idea: Borrowed from neuromorphic event cameras' address-event representation: each row on a glass panel has a sentinel cell with a deliberately weaker capacitor and a thin-film comparator that fires the row address onto an arbitrated event bus when it decays, so only rows that need refresh get it.
why: Refresh (fact 3): oxide-TFT cells rarely leak, so event-driven refresh cuts refresh operations 100x+ versus timed sweeps and removes the refresh counter.

title: Hf: hafnium-zirconia negative-capacitance gate boosts sense-amp gain
idea: Insert a thin HZO ferroelectric in the gate stack of the SA pull-down pair, matched for stabilized negative capacitance so the internal gate swing exceeds the bitline swing (~1.5-2x step-up) during sensing.
why: Pre-amplifies the ~100 mV signal, letting VARY drop below 1 V (fact 10) and SA transistors shrink; claims ~30% lower sensing energy.

title: Time-domain reflectometry reads a whole gain-cell column in one pulse
idea: Box: 2T gain cell (storage node gates read FET) x read-FET loading x TDR echo sensing x controlled-impedance transmission-line bitline x Si x standard BEOL. With all read wordlines of a column enabled, each '1' cell's conducting read FET adds a shunt load at a known position, so one picosecond pulse's echo profile encodes every bit in the column by time of flight.
why: One TDR receiver per column instead of per-segment SAs; 256+ bits per pulse cuts sense energy and periphery count.

title: IBM eDRAM micro-sense-amps built inside each 3D DRAM tier
idea: Failure mined: IBM's deep-trench eDRAM, with 3-transistor micro sense amps on 32-cell local bitlines, died only because GlobalFoundries quit 7 nm. Fix: carry the micro-SA into 3D, with a 3-transistor thin-film micro-SA beside each 16-cell lateral bitline in every tier. Each tier becomes a self-sensing short-bitline array, where a 1 fF planar capacitor still yields ~100 mV.
why: 10x at the same cost: short local bitlines remove the capacitor bottleneck that blocks 3D DRAM (fact 2), and 32-48 tiers of lateral planar cells from shared etches give ~10x bits/mm^2 at ~3D-NAND cost.

title: Dual-mode HZO: linear dielectric daily, ferroelectric only at shutdown
idea: Constraint: non-volatile, without ferroelectric fatigue. The capacitor runs as a sub-coercive high-k DRAM cell during operation; at power-fail, bipolar plate-line drivers pulse +/-Vc row by row so each cell's stored charge sets its polarization, and at power-up a destructive ferroelectric read with a dual-reference SA reloads the charge state.
why: NV plus unlimited daily endurance, since the ferroelectric switches once per power cycle; HZO's k (~30-40) also eases the capacitor wall (fact 1).

title: Driven guard traces hide bitline coupling capacitance
idea: Borrow electrometer active guarding: MAGNIFY the role of shield lines between bitlines by driving each with a unity-gain follower of its neighbor bitline during charge sharing, so bitline-to-neighbor capacitance (~40% of Cbl) sees no voltage change and draws no charge.
why: Fact 1: effective Cbl -30-40%, signal +50-60%, allowing ~35% smaller Cs or lower VARY; followers are shared per 32 bitlines and only active for the ~2 ns window.

title: Dumbwaiter: per-mat vertical bond shafts replace global data buses
idea: A dumbwaiter carries food straight up to each floor instead of through the halls. Give every mat its own column of hybrid bonds to a logic die stacked directly above, so data leaves the local sense amps vertically over ~10 um instead of crossing mm-long global I/O lines, serializers and the PHY.
why: On-die global I/O plus the PHY are ~40-60% of DDR access energy (10-20 pJ/bit, fact 5); a vertical shaft at ~0.05-0.1 pJ/bit cuts per-access energy ~10x for the data path.

title: LCD array-tester voltage imaging replaces on-die test periphery
idea: Borrowed from the LCD fab's electro-optic array tester, a modulator plate that images every pixel's voltage without contact: after the array layer on glass is built, a pattern is written and all cell voltages are imaged to find dead or weak-retention cells before periphery and stacking.
why: Periphery and capital: removes test-mode and BIST circuitry (~2-3% area) and probe cards, and yields full retention maps for refresh binning.

title: Thin-film AlN piezoelectric transformer replaces wordline charge pumps
idea: Substitute switched-capacitor VPP charge pumps with a released thin-film AlN contour-mode piezoelectric transformer that steps 1.1 V to ~3 V at resonance. AlN sputtering, XeF2 release and e-beam electrodes are university-fab processes.
why: Periphery energy and area: piezo transformers can reach >80% conversion efficiency against ~30-50% for multi-stage pumps, cutting wordline supply energy ~2x.

title: Cloud erasure coding lets periphery fabs skip particle cleans
idea: Backblaze runs cheap consumer disks reliably by erasure-coding across them. Group each bank's 16 subarrays with 2 parity subarrays and an on-die Reed-Solomon reconstruct engine in the column path, so a particle-killed subarray is rebuilt on the fly, and the fab removes ~80% of inter-step particle scrubs and megasonic rinses.
why: Water: ~10x higher killer-defect density is tolerated, so particle-removal rinses, a top UPW user, fall ~5-10x at constant yield; parity costs ~12% array area.

title: Eliminate redundancy fuses: spare-free dies with controller-side row retirement
idea: Strip spare rows and columns, eFuse/antifuse banks and repair CAMs from the die. Each die ships a bad-row bitmap measured at wafer test and stored in SPD flash, and the controller remaps failing rows into a reserved 0.5% of normal rows through a 4-way hashed remap table.
why: Removes repair logic and spare arrays (~3-5% of die) plus fuse-programming test time, and takes repair comparators off the decode path (-0.5 ns). Yield holds because remapping is flexible die-wide.

title: Core-rope weaving: per-die e-beam via layer hardwires repairs
idea: Apollo's core-rope ROM was woven by hand, each wire passing through or around each core. After wafer sort at the via-2 level, a maskless multi-beam e-beam writes one custom via layer per die that hardwires spare rows and columns into place. That layer is the one added 'mask', and no physical mask exists.
why: Deletes fuse banks, fuse latches and address-compare logic (~3-5% of die, fact 7) and power-up fuse loading, so repaired addresses take no extra latency.

title: Post-it notes: module controller remaps bad rows, fuses removed
idea: Instead of burning fixes into each die, stick notes on the module: dies ship without e-fuse banks or redundancy-steering comparators, and the CXL/buffer controller keeps a remap table of bad rows and columns found at test (stored in SPD flash) that redirects to spare rows pooled across every die on the module.
why: Periphery area and yield: fuse banks and spare-steering logic are ~3-6% of die; pooling spares at module level also lifts usable-die yield by a few percent.

title: Fuse-free die: redundancy map lives in the controller
idea: Limit: no fuse banks, antifuse arrays or laser repair on the die. At test, failing rows and columns are recorded in a signed table on the module SPD, and the memory controller remaps addresses before issuing them, with spare rows as ordinary rows.
why: Periphery area (-2-3% of the die), removes laser-repair tools (capital), and allows field repair at boot.

title: Idle-time sense-amp offset self-trim tracks aging in field
idea: Each SA gets a 4-bit current-injection trim; during refresh-idle windows it senses equalized bitlines (zero signal) and binary-searches the trim to null offset, re-running monthly so BTI drift at 125 C is continuously cancelled. Trim codes live in a reserved array row, not fuses.
why: Offset (~2,000 e- equivalent on 40 fF) is the real minimum-charge setter; nulling it lets Cs fall ~2x (fact 1) over the full 10-year life.

title: Controller-held repair map replaces on-die fuse banks
idea: Write wafer-test repair results to the module SPD EEPROM; at boot the memory controller loads the bad-row/column map into its own address-translation table and steers accesses to spare rows exposed as ordinary addresses, so the DRAM die drops laser/e-fuse banks and redundancy-compare logic.
why: Periphery (fact 7): ~2-4% die area and ~0.5-1 ns of tRCD, and lets older lines ship dies with more defects (yield up).

title: Asymmetry: per-bitline read inverters, one slow shared write scanner
idea: TRIZ #4 Asymmetry: for read-mostly AI weights and KV-cache, a 2T oxide gain cell is read non-destructively by a single minimum-size inverter per bitline (no latch, no reference, no restore), while writes go through one high-voltage scanning write driver per 64k cells at ~10 us per row.
why: 100x path: read periphery ~10x smaller, write drivers amortized ~1000x, cells stacked 8+ BEOL tiers on mature nodes; trade-offs: writes 100-1000x slower, so it is unsuitable for write-heavy data. Attacks Facts 4 and 7.

title: Kinetic-proofreading two-threshold sensing that heals marginal cells on access
idea: DNA polymerase rejects errors with an energy-spending delay (kinetic proofreading). The sense path samples each bitline against +delta then -delta references. Cells that resolve consistently restore normally. Cells inside the delta band get a boosted-VPP extended restore, and their address goes to a small weak-row table for faster refresh.
why: Fact 3: catches decaying cells during normal traffic before they fail, so baseline refresh can relax ~2x and refresh energy/bandwidth roughly halves.

title: Pair partial-good dies behind a 65nm bank-remap bridge
idea: Instead of scrapping or down-binning dies with dead banks, package two partial-good dies with a small 65 nm bridge chip that presents one standard full-capacity die and routes each bank address to whichever die has it working.
why: Usable supply: recovers ~5-10% of wafer output now scrapped or sold as low density, using only trailing logic and OSAT capacity.

title: Eliminate row decoders: token-passing wordlines for streaming memory tiers
idea: For sequential tiers (AI weights, KV-cache streams, checkpoints), remove the row decoder tree. Each wordline driver holds a one-bit token in a 2-transistor dynamic stage and passes it to the next row on every activate clock, so rows open in a fixed order. A 'jump' tap every 512 rows allows coarse seeks.
why: Removes the row decoder and predecoder (~4-6% of die) and ~15 address wires per mat. Random access is lost but streaming traffic (~80% of weight reads) keeps full bandwidth.

title: Latch resolution time as free confidence signal for decoding
idea: Box: pillar cap x Si access x metastability-timed latch x per-SA time comparator x bulk Si x standard. A tiny counter measures how long each latch takes to resolve; slow resolution (small input) marks the bit low-confidence, giving the decoder soft information without extra reference reads.
why: Soft decoding of 1% raw BER at single-read latency; near-capacity code rates (~0.9) at almost no area.

title: Ice rink: Josephson comparators sense cryogenic DRAM bitlines
idea: Glide without friction: at 4 K, read DRAM bitlines with Josephson-junction quantum-flux-parametron or SFQ comparators that switch on ~1e-19 J, driving superconducting passive lines to the processor, while the DRAM array runs at ~0.3 V with near-zero leakage and no refresh.
why: Sensing and data-movement energy falls by orders of magnitude at the device; even with cryocooler overhead (~400 W/W at 4 K) this aims at ~10x per access for quantum/superconducting computer memory.

title: Coulomb-blockade nanocrystal storage islands read by gain FETs
idea: Molecule-scale jump: 5-20 electrons are stored on a ~3 nm Si or metal nanocrystal between thin tunnel barriers, where charging energy >> kT blocks leakage, and read non-destructively through the threshold shift of an adjacent gain FET; writes use low-field direct tunneling that does not wear the oxide, and no refresh is issued.
why: Retention of ~10^3-10^5 s at nanocapacitor size means zero refresh (fact 3) and no capacitor (fact 1).

title: Al+N: aluminum-nitride piezoelectric transformer generates wordline boost voltage
idea: Replace the multistage capacitive VPP charge pump with a Rosen-type AlN thin-film piezoelectric transformer driven at mechanical resonance from the 1.1 V rail; its 3-5x voltage gain plus a small rectifier gives the 3 V wordline supply without large flying capacitors.
why: Charge pumps occupy notable periphery area at ~30-40% efficiency; piezo step-up could cut pump area ~3x and raise efficiency toward 60%+, trimming the energy of the stuck 3 V wordline swing (fact 10).

title: Automotive-grade MTJ storage holds trims and repair maps
idea: Floating-gate and charge-trap trims lose charge at 125 C, and e-fuses are one-shot. Store sense trims, timing codes and repair addresses in high-barrier MTJs (thermal stability Delta > 80, already qualified for 10 y at 150 C) beside the periphery, rewritable for in-field repair.
why: Enables in-field re-trim/repair at hot; replaces bulky fuse banks (fact 7) with ~10x denser nonvolatile bits.

title: Inkjet-printed conductive links perform redundancy repair at sort
idea: Worse: burn area on fuse banks, antifuse programming pumps and laser-fuse windows. Flip: at wafer sort an inkjet printer deposits silver or copper nanoparticle links on a top-level link field that sets the spare-address compare bits fuses normally hold, programmed straight from the test map.
why: Periphery area (fact 7): deletes ~1-3% of die in fuse area and fuse-read logic with maskless per-die repair.

title: Curvature: wound film memory roll with edge-metallized bitline contacts
idea: TRIZ #14 Spheroidality: like a film capacitor, a 5 um polymer strip carrying nanoimprinted oxide-TFT DRAM arrays is wound into a 1000-turn cylinder; bitlines of every turn run to one edge, where sprayed and laser-patterned end-cap metallization connects them to a CMOS reader disk, so all periphery sits on the circular end face.
why: 100x path: roll-to-roll nanoimprint at ~0.5 um aims at ~80 GB/m2 per layer for ~$5-10/m2 (~$0.1/GB), with the reader disk amortized over 1000 turns; trade-offs: us-ms access, retention needs very low-leakage TFTs and end-cap registration is unproven. Attacks Facts 4 and 7.

title: Sacrificial-polymer air-gap bitlines raise sense transfer ratio
idea: Substitute oxide bitline spacers with vacuum: a sacrificial polymer between bitlines is thermally decomposed through a porous cap, lowering bitline capacitance. Spin-coat, cap and bake steps fit a university fab.
why: Charge wall (fact 1): Cbl drops ~30-40%, raising signal Cs/(Cs+Cbl) ~1.4x, so Cs can shrink or bitlines can lengthen with fewer sense amps.

title: Periphery wafers from U.S. legacy logic fabs
idea: Scale the fab across companies: periphery (~49% of area) is made as a separate 28-40 nm CMOS wafer at U.S. foundries on depreciated tools, only the array wafer needs a DRAM fab, and U.S. OSATs hybrid-bond the two.
why: Halves the EUV/DRAM-fab area needed per bit (facts 4, 7), adds U.S. manufacturing share within ~2 years, and uses capacity that already exists.

title: Battery active balancing recycles bitline charge between subarrays
idea: Like a BMS shuttling charge from full cells to empty ones, a switched flying-capacitor bus links subarrays: when subarray A equalizes its full-swing bitlines, its surplus charge is dumped into subarray B, which is mid-restore. About 40% of restore charge is recycled from the previous activation.
why: Energy per bit/voltage floor: bitline CV2 dominates activation; activate energy falls ~30-40%, as does charge-pump load.

title: MOS-varactor capacitance collapse amplifies bitline signal before latching
idea: Effect: parametric amplification (voltage-dependent capacitance). After charge sharing, drive the bottom plate of an accumulation-mode MOS varactor on each bitline into depletion so bitline capacitance falls ~3x; charge is conserved, so the differential voltage grows ~3x (V=Q/C) with no DC current before the latch fires.
why: Sense margin (facts 1, 7): ~3x signal allows 2x longer bitlines (half as many SA stripes) or ~2x smaller Cs.

title: IGZO shadow row buffers magnify open rows eightfold
idea: Stack 2T0C IGZO gain-cell latches (<=350 C; leakage <1e-18 A, so they hold for seconds) above each SA stripe, giving every bank 8 shadow row buffers that keep recently opened rows readable without re-activation.
why: Facts 8 and 9: activations fall ~30-50% for AI access patterns, cutting overfetch energy and row-hammer exposure, with zero added silicon area.

title: BEOL oxide-TFT sub-wordline drivers stacked over the array
idea: Move sub-wordline driver strips out of silicon into a back-end thin-film transistor layer directly above the mats (wide-bandgap channel, high off-resistance suits 3 V switching), so the substrate under the array returns to cells or sense amps.
why: Periphery footprint (fact 7): ~10-15% die area freed without hybrid bonding.

title: On-die microheaters anneal aging sense amps back to health
idea: Ideal result: periphery that resets its own wear. Polysilicon microheaters under SA stripes and drivers heat local transistors to ~250 C for seconds during maintenance windows, recovering BTI and hot-carrier threshold shifts.
why: Lifetime and offset (facts 1, 7): keeps SA offsets near day-zero for years, allowing tighter margins and longer service life.

title: Self-timed sense amps signal completion, absorbing mature-node variation
idea: Reverse the timing source: each SA group raises a dual-rail done flag when its latch has regenerated and the bank proceeds when all flags are up, so periphery built at U.S. 28-40 nm fabs runs at typical rather than worst-case speed.
why: Fact 7 and U.S. manufacturability: ~30% timing guardband removed, making mature U.S. nodes viable for DRAM periphery.

title: Magnifying glass: one-transistor local preamp every sixteen cells
idea: A magnifying glass enlarges the signal before the eye sees it: split each bitline into 16-cell local segments of ~1 fF; the cell shares charge with this tiny segment (about +/-300 mV), which drives the gate of one segment transistor that discharges the long global bitline, while a separate write-back transistor restores.
why: Capacitor wall (fact 1): transfer ratio rises from ~0.1 to ~0.8, so Cs can drop to ~1 fF (AR ~15:1) and 3D tiers can use tiny capacitors; costs 2 transistors per 16 cells (~10% array overhead).
